rules.preferred: Covers information in any form (written, oral, visual) that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential.
rules.fallback: Written information marked confidential, plus oral information identified as confidential at disclosure and confirmed in writing within 30 days.
rules.never: Only written information that is marked confidential.
rules.guidance: Narrowing the definition removes protection for demos and calls, which is where most of our disclosures happen.

rules.preferred: The four standard exclusions only: public without breach, previously known, received from a third party without restriction, independently developed.
rules.never: Any exclusion beyond the four standard ones.
rules.guidance: Extra exclusions are usually residuals clauses in disguise.

rules.preferred: Five years after the last disclosure; trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.
rules.fallback: Three years after the last disclosure, trade secret carve-out must stay.
rules.never: Less than three years, or deleting the trade secret carve-out.
rules.guidance: The trade secret carve-out matters for protection under the German GeschGehG.

rules.never: Any right to use information retained in unaided memory.
rules.guidance: A residuals clause effectively licenses our know-how. Red line.

rules.preferred: No non-solicitation or no-hire obligations in an NDA.
rules.guidance: Out of scope for an NDA; no-hire clauses also raise employment and competition law issues.

rules.preferred: No cap on liability for breach of confidentiality.
rules.fallback: Cap at the higher of EUR 250,000 or the contract value, excluding intent and gross negligence.
rules.never: A cap below EUR 250,000 or an exclusion of liability for breach of confidentiality.
rules.guidance: Under German law, liability for intent cannot be excluded in advance (§ 276(3) BGB).

rules.preferred: German law; exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Berlin.
rules.fallback: German law; DIS arbitration seated in Frankfurt am Main.
rules.guidance: Our client has no capacity to litigate abroad.

rules.preferred: Return or destroy within 14 days of request and confirm in writing.
rules.fallback: Within 30 days; copies in automatic backups may be kept if they stay confidential until deleted in the ordinary course.
rules.guidance: Backup carve-outs are market standard if the confidentiality obligation continues.

rules.preferred: Express right to seek injunctive relief.
rules.guidance: Interim injunctions (einstweilige Verfügung) are the only remedy that works fast enough.
